newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine two-year note coupon rises to 11.50 pct.
newsitem.headline: Philippine two-year note coupon rises to 11.50 pct.

text.p: The coupon rate on the Philippine two-year Treasury note rose to 11.50 percent at the auction on Tuesday from 11.25 percent last month, the Bureau of Treasury said.
The average rate rose to 11.26 percent from 11.082 percent. Accepted rates were from 10.75 to 11.50 percent.
The auction drew 6.76 billion pesos worth of bids, of which three billion pesos were awarded.
The government was supposed to sell a total of 4.0 billion pesos of the notes but decided to accept less because of some high bids.
"They (the auction committee) viewed the rates as something off-market," Bureau of Treasury director Juanchito Dispo told Reuters on Tuesday after the auction.
Traders said the rise in the two-year note had been expected after Treasury bill rates reversed its downtrend on Monday after weeks of decline.
The Central Bank had wanted interest rates not to move lower when it started to sell late last week six-month reverse repos at a higher-than-market rate of 10.125 percent.
The Central Bank's move was intended to soak up liquidity in the system to prevent inflationary expectations, a government official had said.
